title: Customer-service automation: a buildable pilot blueprint
question: What must TMF scope, build and verify to offer a premium customer-service automation pilot?
summary: Proposed offer: assess the current support workflow, then pilot one inbound text channel and a small approved intent set with reliable human takeover. Own the durable case, permissions, recovery and operating evidence. Reuse channel/routing infrastructure; expand voice and financial actions only after separate scoping. Research pack is useful for discovery and build planning; service implementation and commercial demand remain unproven.

findings.text: Public replies and private notes share the comment model. New comments are submitted through ticket create/update, not a comment-create endpoint. Displayed author and authenticated updater can differ.
findings.label: documented

findings.text: Comment bodies above 64 kB can be truncated without an error. Attachment URLs can lead outside the vendor host; credentials must not follow them to third parties.
findings.label: documented

findings.text: Webhook delivery can duplicate or omit events. The documented invocation log covers seven days. An integration needs durable reconciliation beyond that window.
findings.label: documented
findings.caveat: Reconciliation is our proposed response to the documented delivery limits.

findings.text: A routing Task is not the durable customer case: rejected or timed-out reservations can return a task to pending; terminal task records are deleted after five minutes.
findings.label: documented

findings.text: Task updates support ETag/If-Match checks and return 412 on version mismatch. Updating attributes and moving a task to wrapping/completed requires separate requests.
findings.label: documented

findings.text: Reservations are offers to a worker. A reservation that receives no handling decision within its workflow timeout leaves the task available for other workers.
findings.label: documented

findings.text: Twilio recommends SDK request-signature validation, accounting for the exact webhook URL and all received parameters rather than a frozen field list.
findings.label: documented

findings.text: Stripe API v1 retains the first executed response for a key, including 500 responses; keys may be pruned after at least 24 hours. Reusing a pruned key can create a new operation.
findings.label: documented

findings.text: Selected SDK modules serialize task assignmentStatus, reservation reservationStatus and If-Match headers; task and reservation are distinct resource wrappers.
findings.label: observed
findings.caveat: REA parsed selected inert release files; direct source readback confirmed these fields. This does not validate the remote API or complete SDK.

findings.text: A sellable first offer is an assessment plus a narrow assisted-service pilot, followed by separately scoped managed operations. Demand and willingness to pay remain untested.
findings.label: proposed

requirements.text: Validate provider webhook signatures before admitting work
requirements.acceptance: Tampered body, wrong URL and invalid signature each create no case or action; valid vendor fixtures pass.

requirements.text: Persist and deduplicate incoming events by tenant, provider and external event identity
requirements.acceptance: Replaying one event 20 times yields one case effect; same identifier in another tenant stays independent.

requirements.text: Keep a durable case independent of temporary routing resources
requirements.acceptance: Expired/deleted task still leaves full case history, owner and unresolved customer request visible.

requirements.text: Verify customer identity before revealing account-specific information
requirements.acceptance: Unverified sender gets generic help; mismatched account cannot retrieve another customer order.

requirements.text: Enforce tenant and record permissions across retrieval, tools and exports
requirements.acceptance: Adversarial cross-tenant identifiers and disallowed knowledge return denial without data exposure.

requirements.text: Set public/private visibility explicitly on every comment action
requirements.acceptance: Internal-note content never appears in customer reply, retrieval context for that customer or exported transcript.

requirements.text: Preserve actor, displayed author and authenticated updater separately
requirements.acceptance: Audit readback distinguishes the service account from the employee shown as author.

requirements.text: Check reply size and attachment destination before sending
requirements.acceptance: Oversized body is held for editing; external attachment fetch sends no vendor credentials and obeys size/type limits.

requirements.text: Use approved versioned knowledge with owner, access scope and expiry
requirements.acceptance: Expired or inaccessible article is excluded; an answer records the article version supporting it.

requirements.text: Escalate unsupported answers and hostile instructions in customer content
requirements.acceptance: A request to ignore policy cannot expand tool authority; absent evidence yields a handoff rather than invented policy.

requirements.text: Model queue, routing task and reservation as separate linked records
requirements.acceptance: Rejected reservation remains in history and a new offer links to the same unresolved case.

requirements.text: Confirm acceptance before treating a human handoff as complete
requirements.acceptance: Timeout/no available worker leaves a named queue owner and fallback callback task; customer sees an accurate pending state.

requirements.text: Fence automated replies as soon as human takeover is committed
requirements.acceptance: Concurrent queued bot send and takeover permit no bot send after the takeover version commits.

requirements.text: Re-read and resolve version conflicts before changing task state
requirements.acceptance: Stale If-Match gets 412; newer owner/state survives and operator receives the conflict.

requirements.text: Configure skills, capacity, business hours, overflow and abandonment rules
requirements.acceptance: After-hours, full-capacity and abandoned-request scenarios preserve a recoverable case and correct destination.

requirements.text: Persist outbound intent and use an idempotent dispatch boundary
requirements.acceptance: Crash before send, during send and after acknowledgment is recovered without claiming unconfirmed delivery.

requirements.text: Represent ambiguous provider outcomes explicitly and reconcile them
requirements.acceptance: A send timeout records outcome unknown; readback or human resolution establishes its result before retry.

requirements.text: Keep money-moving actions outside the first pilot; design their approval contract
requirements.acceptance: Refund request captures order, amount, currency and responsible owner, but cannot execute a refund in pilot.

requirements.text: Scope future payment idempotency to provider API version and operation identity
requirements.acceptance: For an approved future refund, changed parameters cannot reuse a key; pruned-key and repeated-500 recovery uses authoritative lookup.

requirements.text: Reconcile missed events using provider-supported read APIs and checkpoints
requirements.acceptance: A deliberately omitted webhook is recovered from a known fixture; checkpoint advances only after durable application.

requirements.text: Bound retries, record dead letters and provide an operator recovery queue
requirements.acceptance: Persistent provider failure ends in visible manual recovery with attempt history, without silently dropping the case.

requirements.text: Treat multi-request task completion as a recoverable workflow
requirements.acceptance: Failure between attribute update and completion does not mark the case resolved; recovery reads both outcomes.

requirements.text: Use managed secret references, least privilege and rotation
requirements.acceptance: Revoked integration credential stops actions visibly; replacement succeeds without credentials in receipts or exports.

requirements.text: Record append-only action history with retention and redacted logs
requirements.acceptance: Case owner can reconstruct each action and decision; retention deletion removes scoped content with an auditable receipt.

requirements.text: Define SLA clocks, pause reasons, timezone and escalation owner
requirements.acceptance: Weekend, daylight-saving and waiting-on-customer fixtures match the signed service schedule.

requirements.text: Measure successful resolution separately from bot response or handoff
requirements.acceptance: Dashboard reports eligible cases, repeat contacts, acceptance failures, confirmed delivery and correction rate with clear denominators.

requirements.text: Provide kill switch, export, restore and vendor outage runbook
requirements.acceptance: Operator disables automated sends, restores a fixture backup and resumes only after reconciliation.

requirements.text: Gate pilot on evaluated cases and actual sandbox workflows
requirements.acceptance: Signed pilot corpus includes happy path, ambiguity, wrong identity, stale policy, duplicate, omission, timeout, race and unavailable human; no unexplained high-risk failures.

requirements.text: Sign scope, authoritative systems, dependencies and support ownership
requirements.acceptance: Client approves included intents/channels, integration access, exceptions, data handling and exit deliverables before go-live.

requirements.text: Establish baseline volumes and a costed pilot budget
requirements.acceptance: Client inputs measured eligible volume, handling time, provider usage and QA/support effort; budget states uncertainty and stop threshold.

requirements.text: Scope voice, recording, telecom and jurisdiction obligations separately
requirements.acceptance: Before voice launch, responsible owner records applicable consent, recording, number/channel provisioning and specialist decisions for each served location.

requirements.text: Assess assurance and sector obligations against actual customer requirements
requirements.acceptance: Procurement/data classification review identifies requested attestations, contractual controls and any specialist signoff; no certification is inferred from vendor selection.

unknowns: No customer interview, current buying intent or willingness-to-pay validation; this is a researched service blueprint, not market proof.
Client identity, jurisdiction, channel mix, monthly volume, peak load, languages and accessibility requirements remain unspecified.
Authoritative case system, account identity proof, approved knowledge corpus and allowed automatic intents require client selection.
Vendor plan entitlements, scopes, rate limits, export coverage and current pricing have not been verified in an authenticated tenant.
No sandbox email/chat/voice delivery, real handoff, refund, intrusion assessment, disaster recovery or production customer-service flow was run.
Privacy, retention, recording, sector obligations and requested assurance need a scoped client review; this report establishes no legal or certification conclusion.
Research was performed by an operator using web tools and the real REA repo. The project CLI validated/rendered evidence; it did not autonomously find or assess sources.
No independent second reviewer checked every claim. Source availability and structural validation do not establish semantic support.
General-purpose deep-research orchestration, browser acquisition, source snapshots, semantic review and integrated Craft adapters remain unimplemented in the core tool.
